promise: Complete a bounded desktop task through observed controls and verify the resulting state.
audience: People and agents operating desktop applications.
trigger: Operate an application through an available computer-use surface.

modes.name: Plan
modes.when: The task spans several app states.
modes.output: An observable target and bounded action plan.

modes.name: Operate
modes.when: The target and authorization are clear.

modes.name: Recover
modes.when: The action result is ambiguous or blocked.
modes.output: A fresh observation, safe recovery or explicit stop.

examples.title: Confirm a changed sort order
examples.brief: Use Desktop Tasks to change the sort order in a fictional task app to newest first. First name the visible success condition. Use fresh observed controls, verify the resulting order and report any step you cannot confirm.
examples.before: An automation clicks a remembered button location and assumes a form saved.
examples.after: A fresh labeled target and the saved-state confirmation establish what changed.
examples.why: Observed post-state separates an attempted interaction from completed work.

boundaries: Real desktop execution requires an available host tool and platform permissions; the fixture is a simulation.

verification.name: Functional acceptance
verification.expected: Supplied fictional tasks exercise actual mechanisms and failure boundaries.
verification.evidence: 143 native tests passed; fixture/backend tests do not establish OS permission or live task acceptance.

verification.name: Native host acceptance
verification.expected: Actual provider/host/desktop/daemon/runner acceptance for the selected adapter.
verification.evidence: No live model, real desktop transaction, invitation, deployment or production data migration was performed by this functional baseline.

sources.role: Primary retained owner history, mechanisms and records; portable method consolidates the listed entry points.

consolidation: One portable method entry with mode references; original native engines, agents and records retained as optional adapters.
publication_status: Installation and evidence scopes are documented below.

marketing.headline: Finish the task. Check the screen that proves it.
marketing.lead: For people asking an agent to work in desktop apps. Desktop Tasks makes the agent use observed controls, stay within a clear action budget and verify the final state before calling the work complete.

benefits.title: Know whether it worked
benefits.body: Separate a click that was attempted from a change that was actually visible afterward.

benefits.title: Recover from uncertain screens
benefits.body: Re-observe when labels and pixels disagree, and stop repeated actions from compounding an ambiguous result.

benefits.title: Use the tools you already have
benefits.body: Apply the method through an available host computer-use tool; install the native adapter only if needed.

walkthrough.title: Name the finish line
walkthrough.detail: Specify the application, authorized change and visible state that would establish success.

walkthrough.title: Operate from fresh evidence
walkthrough.detail: Identify a labeled control, compare it with the current screen and act through the host tool.

walkthrough.title: Verify or recover
walkthrough.detail: Read the resulting state. Refresh an uncertain step within the agreed budget and report partial completion plainly.

use_when: You need an agent to complete a bounded task in a desktop application.
A click can succeed without saving the intended change.
A workflow needs explicit recovery and stop conditions.
not_for: Granting desktop permissions or supplying a missing computer-use tool.
marketing.quickstart_prompt: Use Desktop Tasks to change the sort order in a fictional task app to newest first. First name the visible success condition. Use fresh observed controls, verify the resulting order and report any step you cannot confirm.
marketing.output_preview:
Task: show newest items first
Observed: sort menu offers “Newest first”
Attempted: selected that option
Verified: selected label changed; top item has the newest date
Remaining: none within this bounded task

If the list did not change: refresh the observation before another action.
marketing.example_note: Fictional interaction receipt. No real application was operated to create this illustration.
install_notes: Python 3.11 or later is required by the portable install/build helper. The installed method runs through your agent host.
The method needs an agent host with computer-use tools and the necessary OS permissions.
The optional tool-cua package supplies platform backends; fixture tests alone do not establish live desktop access.
Installing the skill does not change application state.
marketing.proof_summary: Native backend and fixture checks cover action plumbing and recovery logic. Live OS permissions and a successful task in your selected application remain a separate check.
marketing.next_step: Choose one small app task with an unmistakable visible finish line.
